payload.summary: Three ready-to-assign activities for grades 6 to 8: an argument essay, a plant-growth investigation and a ratios problem set. A teacher adds any of them to a class as a draft, then edits it before publishing.
payload.title: Middle school starter pack

codex.body:
1. State your claim in the first paragraph.
2. Give each reason its own paragraph, with evidence.
3. Name a counterargument and explain why your claim still holds.
4. End by restating your claim in new words.
codex.title: Argument checklist

template.overview: Students take a position on whether phones should be allowed in class and support it with reasons and evidence, then answer the strongest point on the other side.
template.prompt: Should students be allowed to use phones in class? Write an argument that states your claim, gives at least two reasons with evidence, and responds to one counterargument.
template.subject: english-language-arts
template.title: Should phones be allowed in class?

template.analysisPrompt: What pattern do you see between hours of light and height? Use numbers from your table, and name one thing that could have affected your results.
template.methodPrompt: Describe your setup: how many seedlings, how much light each group gets, and what you kept the same for every group (water, soil, pot size, temperature).
template.overview: Students grow bean seedlings under different amounts of light for two weeks, measure them, and explain what their data shows.
template.question: How does the amount of light a bean seedling gets each day affect how tall it grows in two weeks?
template.subject: science
template.title: How does light affect plant growth?

template.overview: Students scale recipes up and down using equivalent ratios and unit rates.

problems.prompt: A pancake recipe uses 2 cups of flour for every 3 eggs. How many eggs do you need for 8 cups of flour?
Lemonade is made with 1 cup of lemon juice for every 5 cups of water. How much water goes with 3.5 cups of lemon juice?
A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of rice. How much rice do you need for 10 people?
Store A sells 6 granola bars for $4.50. Store B sells 10 for $7.00. Which is the better deal per bar? Explain.

template.subject: mathematics
template.title: Ratios in recipes

content.description: Three activities that each work in a single class period or a short unit, written to be edited: change the prompt, the due date or the AI-help level before you publish.
content.title: Middle school starter pack
